topic.title: Stochastic Optimization Guarantees and Robustness
topic.overview: Stochastic optimizers learn from noisy gradient estimates, so convergence depends on step sizes, noise tails, objective geometry, and data access. This cluster develops upper and lower complexity bounds alongside practical estimators and update rules. Heavy-tailed noise, biased gradients, nonconvex objectives, and minimax problems test where familiar SGD intuitions remain valid.
topic.whyItMatters: Reliable optimization requires more than average progress on a favorable benchmark. High-probability guarantees and lower bounds clarify which failures are preventable and which reflect fundamental limits imposed by noise or available information.
topic.evolution: Representatives move from mirror-descent aggregation and oracle lower bounds in the 2000s toward sharper nonconvex and heavy-tail analyses. Recent examples examine constant-step stationary behavior and weakly convex objectives. A 2026 shuffling study also connects statistical convergence with memory-transfer costs, showing that data access can matter alongside iteration counts.
openQuestions: Can adaptive methods attain strong tail guarantees without knowing the noise distribution?
How should optimization complexity jointly account for gradient queries and data movement?
